A morphism of schemes $f:Z\to X$ is an **immersion**, also called a
**locally closed immersion**, if there exist an open subscheme
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ ([[def-open-immersion-schemes]]) and a closed immersion
$i:Z\to U$ ([[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]) with $f=j\circ i$. A factorization
is a device exhibiting $f$, not extra data attached to it: whether $f$ is an
immersion is a property of the morphism $f$ alone, and closed immersions
($U=X$) and open immersions (with $i$ an isomorphism onto $U$) are immersions.

A morphism $f:X\to S$ is **quasi-compact** if $f^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact for
every quasi-compact open $V\subseteq S$. It is **quasi-separated** if, for
affine opens $U,U'\subseteq X$ lying over a common affine open of $S$, the
intersection $U\cap U'$ is quasi-compact. This affine criterion is the
definition used here, before the diagonal construction is available.

A morphism $i:Z\to X$ is a **closed immersion** if its underlying map is a
homeomorphism onto a closed subset and the morphism
$\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$ is surjective.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$, its **scheme-theoretic image**, when it exists, is
the smallest closed subscheme $Z\hookrightarrow Y$ through which $f$ factors.
Existence is not part of this definition.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
Jacobian-criterion, ample-powers, Chern-form and comparison suppliers below.
Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex scheme of pure dimension $n\ge0$.

Then the closed points of $X$ carry a structure of **complex manifold**
$X^{\mathrm{an}}$, its **analytification**: if $X\ne\varnothing$ and $n\ge1$
this is a compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth complex manifold of complex
dimension $n$
([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]); if $n=0$ it is the
finite discrete set $X(\mathbb C)$ with its unique complex structure in the
convention of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]; and if
$X=\varnothing$ then $X^{\mathrm{an}}=\varnothing$. Every standard smooth
algebraic chart of $X$ becomes a holomorphic chart of $X^{\mathrm{an}}$, and
every morphism of smooth complex schemes $X\to Y$ induces a holomorphic map
$X^{\mathrm{an}}\to Y^{\mathrm{an}}$.

Moreover, for every ample invertible sheaf $A$ on $X$ there is a smooth
positive closed real $(1,1)$-form $\eta_A$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ whose de Rham
class is the real image of the topological first Chern class
$c_1(A):=c_1(A^{\mathrm{an}})\in H^2(X^{\mathrm{an}};\mathbb Z)$:
$$J_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}[\eta_A]=\rho_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\bigl(c_1(A)\bigr),$$
where $J$ is the de Rham comparison and $\rho$ the change of coefficients
$\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R$
([[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]]).
In dimension $n=0$ and for $X=\varnothing$ every $2$-form and every degree-two
cohomology class is zero and $\eta_A=0$, so the identity holds trivially.

Let $X$ be a classical algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of
[[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]: a separated
quasi-compact locally ringed space over $\mathbb C$ with a finite cover by
affine models $Z\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, the morphisms being the regular maps,
i.e. the morphisms of locally ringed spaces over $\mathbb C$
([[def-morphism-locally-ringed-spaces]]).

(a) **Analytic topology.** An affine model $Z\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ carries the
subspace topology of the Euclidean topology of $\mathbb C^n$
([[lem-metrics-on-rn]], [[def-metric-topology]],
[[rem-complex-euclidean-space-dictionary]],
[[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]). If $Z_1,Z_2\subseteq X$ are affine
models and $\varphi:Z_1\to Z_2$ is the structure-sheaf isomorphism, then on
$Z_1\cap Z_2$ the maps $\varphi$ and $\varphi^{-1}$ are given locally by
polynomial quotient functions
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]) and are
therefore continuous for the Euclidean topologies: polynomial functions are
continuous, and a quotient is continuous wherever its denominator does not
vanish ([[lem-algebra-of-continuous-real-maps-on-a-space]],
[[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]]). Hence the topologies transported
from the two affine models agree on the overlap, so the affine-model topologies
glue to a unique topology on the underlying set of $X$
([[def-topological-space]], [[def-subspace-topology-top]]): the **analytic
topology** of $X$. Every regular map of complex classical varieties is
continuous for the analytic topologies, by the same local description
([[def-continuous-map-top]]), and the analytic topology refines the Zariski
topology because polynomial zero sets are Euclidean closed. Whenever a complex
algebraic variety is used as a topological space below it carries the analytic
topology, and each subvariety carries the subspace topology.

(b) **Smooth points.** Let $S$ be a classical variety over $\mathbb C$ and let
$x\in S$. The point $x$ is a **smooth point of $S$** if its algebraic local ring
$\mathcal O_{S,x}$ is a regular local ring: a nonzero Noetherian local ring
whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_x$ satisfies
$\dim_{\mathbb C}(\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2)=\dim\mathcal O_{S,x}$
([[def-embedding-dimension-and-regular-local-ring]]). The residue field at a
classical complex point is $\mathbb C$. The variety $S$ is **smooth** if every
point is smooth. This intrinsic algebraic condition does not require a Zariski
neighbourhood to be algebraically isomorphic to an open subset of affine space.

$X=\coprod_{\alpha\in A}S_\alpha$ into pairwise disjoint nonempty connected

subvariety of $X$; and such that for every $\alpha$ the closure
$\overline{S_\alpha}$ of $S_\alpha$ in $X$ is a union of strata. The latter is
the **frontier condition**: the frontier
$\overline{S_\alpha}\setminus S_\alpha$ of every stratum is a union of strata
([[def-connected-space]], [[def-interior-closure-boundary-top]]).

**The induced structure is the polynomial-quotient function sheaf, not a
restriction of $\mathcal O_X$.** A locally closed $S\subseteq X$ is, locally
inside an affine model $Z\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, the set of points with $h\neq0$

([[def-constructible-subset-variety]],
[[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]); the map

identification: locally functions of the form $a/b$ with $b$ nonvanishing on the
set. The ambient restriction $\mathcal O_X|_S$ is not used, since already at the
origin of the affine line the ambient stalk is the local ring of the line while
the stalk of the reduced point is $\mathbb C$. An open subset of an affine model
is a union of principal open subsets, and each principal open subset is again an
affine model, so every locally closed subvariety of $X$ is a classical variety
for the induced structure sheaf. No existence theorem for stratifications, no
common-refinement theorem and no choice principle is asserted: nothing is
selected, and all cited suppliers are choice-free.

Throughout this page, assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]): the
analytic and cohomological suppliers invoked by the results below assume full

**(1) Compact Kähler manifolds.** Let $n\ge1$. A **Kähler manifold** is a complex
manifold $X$ of complex dimension $n$
([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]) with complex structure
$J$ and a **Hermitian metric** $g$ — a Riemannian metric
([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]) satisfying
$g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)$ for all tangent vectors $v,w$ — whose **real fundamental form**
$\omega(v,w)=g(Jv,w)$ is

- a smooth real 2-form, the section of $\Lambda^2T^*X$ obtained by alternating
  $g(J\cdot,\cdot)$;
- **positive**: $\omega(v,Jv)=g(Jv,Jv)>0$ for every nonzero tangent vector $v$;
- **closed**: $d\omega=0$.

The manifold is **compact Kähler** when the topological space $X$ is compact.

**Orientation.** For a complex basis $(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ of a tangent space $T_xX$,
the ordered real basis $(v_1,Jv_1,\dots,v_n,Jv_n)$ is declared **positive**. This
is well defined: two complex bases differ by a complex-linear automorphism, whose
real determinant is the square of the modulus of its complex determinant and so
is positive, and the local orientations therefore glue along holomorphic charts
to a global orientation of $X$. Let $v_1,\dots,v_n$ be a $g$-orthonormal complex
frame, so that $g(v_j,v_k)=\delta_{jk}$, and let $e_j=g(v_j,\cdot)$ and
$f_j=g(Jv_j,\cdot)$ be the metric-dual covectors. Then
$(e_1,f_1,\dots,e_n,f_n)$ is a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe,
$f_j=-Je_j$ for the pullback action $(J\alpha)(v)=\alpha(Jv)$ of $J$ on
covectors, and

$$\omega=\sum_{j=1}^n e_j\wedge f_j .$$

The **oriented volume form** is the top form

$$dV:=\frac{\omega^n}{n!}=e_1\wedge f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_n\wedge f_n ,$$

which evaluates to $1$ on each positively oriented $g$-orthonormal frame.

**Complex dimension zero.** For $n=0$ a complex manifold is a discrete space and
compactness makes it a finite set of points with its unique complex structure;
there are no tangent vectors and no forms of positive degree, $\omega=0$, and the
operators $L,\Lambda,\partial,\bar\partial,d,\partial^*,\bar\partial^*,d^*$ and
all Laplacians introduced below are zero. The Hodge star is the identity on
degree zero, and $dV$ is the counting measure.

**(2) Complex-valued forms and Kähler operators.** Let $X$ be compact Kähler.
Write $\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)$ for the complex-valued smooth $k$-forms, the
complex-linear extension of the real forms of
[[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]; the Hodge star $*$ of
[[def-riemannian-hodge-star]] extends complex-linearly, and for
$\alpha,\beta\in\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)$ the **integral inner product**

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle=\int_X\alpha\wedge*\bar\beta$$

is complex-linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second; the
integral is that of
[[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-top-form-on-an-oriented-manifold]] and
the integrand is $\lvert\alpha\rvert^2\,dV$ when $\beta=\alpha$, so the pairing
is a positive definite Hermitian form. In holomorphic charts

$$\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\Omega^{p,q}(X),\qquad d=\partial+\bar\partial ,$$

with $\partial$ and $\bar\partial$ of bidegree $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$
([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]]); the decomposition is independent
of the holomorphic chart because holomorphic chart changes preserve bidegree.

Put $L=\omega\wedge$, so that $L:\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)\to\Omega^{k+2}(X;\mathbb C)$,
and let $\Lambda,\partial^*,\bar\partial^*,d^*$ be the formal adjoints of
$L,\partial,\bar\partial,d$ with respect to $\langle\,,\rangle$; existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]], applied
to the bundle of complex-valued forms with the metric of
[[prop-riemannian-metrics-induce-metrics-on-dual-tensor-and-exterior-bundles]]
and the density $dV$. The **Laplacians** are

$$\Delta_d=dd^*+d^*d,\qquad \Delta_\partial=\partial\partial^*+\partial^*\partial,\qquad \Delta_{\bar\partial}=\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial ,$$

and $\epsilon(k)=(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}$.

**(3) Rational pure Hodge structures.** Let $k\in\mathbb Z$. A **rational pure
Hodge structure of weight $k$** is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-vector space
$V$ together with a direct-sum decomposition by $\mathbb C$-subspaces

$$V_{\mathbb C}=V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}V^{p,q},\qquad \overline{V^{p,q}}=V^{q,p},$$

where conjugation is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear involution
$v\otimes\lambda\mapsto v\otimes\bar\lambda$. The sum is finite because
$V_{\mathbb C}$ is finite dimensional, and it is direct by definition. The **Weil
operator** $C$ is the $\mathbb C$-linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathbb C}$ acting
as $i^{p-q}$ on $V^{p,q}$; the conjugation symmetry makes $C$ commute with
conjugation, so $C$ is the complexification of a $\mathbb Q$-linear endomorphism
of $V$.

A **polarization** of such a Hodge structure is a nondegenerate $\mathbb Q$-bilinear
form $Q:V\times V\to\mathbb Q$, extended $\mathbb C$-bilinearly to $V_{\mathbb C}$,
such that

- $Q(y,x)=(-1)^kQ(x,y)$ for all $x,y$;
- $Q(V^{p,q},V^{a,b})=0$ unless $(a,b)=(q,p)$;
- $h(x,y)=Q(Cx,\bar y)$ is a positive definite Hermitian form on $V_{\mathbb C}$.

A **rational sub-Hodge structure** is a $\mathbb Q$-subspace
$U\subseteq V$ with $U_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}(U_{\mathbb C}\cap V^{p,q})$.
The **Tate shift** $V(-r)$, for $r\in\mathbb Z$, keeps the underlying $\mathbb Q$-vector
space, the Weil operator and $Q$ as they are and moves the bidegrees to
$(p+r,q+r)$, so that the weight becomes $k+2r$; equivalently, $(V(-r))^{p,q}=V^{p-r,q-r}$.

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ be open. Write $\Omega^k(U;\mathbb C)$ for smooth
complex-valued $k$-forms. For increasing multi-indices
$I=(i_1<\cdots<i_p)$ and $J=(j_1<\cdots<j_q)$, write
$dz^I=dz_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dz_{i_p}$ and
$d\bar z^J=d\bar z_{j_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge d\bar z_{j_q}$. The invertible
change of cotangent basis
$dz_j=dx_j+i\,dy_j$, $d\bar z_j=dx_j-i\,dy_j$ gives the direct sum
decomposition

$$\Omega^k(U;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\Omega^{p,q}(U),\qquad \Omega^{p,q}(U)=\left\{\sum_{I,J}a_{I,J}(z)\,dz^I\wedge d\bar z^J:a_{I,J}\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb C)\right\},$$

where $0\le p,q\le n$ and every sum is finite. On a $(p,q)$ form
$\eta=\sum_{I,J}a_{I,J}dz^I\wedge d\bar z^J$, define

$$\partial\eta=\sum_{I,J,j}(\partial_{z_j}a_{I,J})\,dz_j\wedge dz^I\wedge d\bar z^J,\qquad \bar\partial\eta=\sum_{I,J,j}(\partial_{\bar z_j}a_{I,J})\,d\bar z_j\wedge dz^I\wedge d\bar z^J.$$

Repeated differentials vanish by alternation; components outside the range
$0\le p,q\le n$ are zero. These operators are the components of $d$ of
bidegrees $(p+1,q)$ and $(p,q+1)$.

Fix $m\ge1$, read $\mathbb C^m$ through
[[rem-complex-euclidean-space-dictionary]], and let $U\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be
open and $a\in U$.

A map $L:\mathbb C^m\to\mathbb C$ is **$\mathbb C$-linear** when
$L(u+v)=L(u)+L(v)$ and $L(\lambda u)=\lambda L(u)$ for all $u,v\in\mathbb C^m$
and **all $\lambda\in\mathbb C$**, the vector-space operations being those of
[[def-vector-space]] over the field $\mathbb C$
([[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]]). Requiring the second clause only for real
$\lambda$ gives the strictly weaker notion of an $\mathbb R$-linear map
([[def-euclidean-linear-map]]) read through the dictionary.

A function $f:U\to\mathbb C$ is **complex differentiable at $a$** when there is a
$\mathbb C$-linear $L:\mathbb C^m\to\mathbb C$ with

$$f(a+h)=f(a)+L(h)+r(h),\qquad \frac{|r(h)|}{\lVert h\rVert}\longrightarrow0 \ \text{ as } h\to0,$$

the quotient being considered for $h\ne0$ with $a+h\in U$ and the norm being that
of the dictionary ([[def-norm-and-normed-space]]). The map $f$ is **holomorphic
on $U$** when it is complex differentiable at every point of $U$.

**Such an $L$ is unique**, so the notation $Df(a):=L$ is well posed. If $L_1$ and
$L_2$ both satisfy the condition, then $T=L_1-L_2$ is $\mathbb C$-linear and
$|T(h)|/\lVert h\rVert\to0$; fixing $h\ne0$ and taking $h$ replaced by $th$ for
real $t\in(0,1)$ small enough that $a+th\in U$, $\mathbb C$-linearity gives
$|T(h)|/\lVert h\rVert=|T(th)|/\lVert th\rVert$, whose limit as $t\to0$ is $0$;
so $T(h)=0$ for every $h$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold $M$, possibly with boundary, integration on smooth simplices followed by the inverse of restriction from continuous to smooth singular cohomology gives a natural isomorphism of unital graded real algebras
$$J_M:H^*_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^*_{\mathrm{sing}}(M;\mathbb R).$$
The source product is wedge of form classes, the target product is the front/back singular cup product, and both stars denote direct sums of the homogeneous groups. Naturality is for smooth maps. No compactness assumption is imposed.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

Assume AC. For a compact Kähler manifold $X$ in the sense of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], every de
Rham class has a unique smooth harmonic representative and
$$H^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(X),\qquad \overline{H^{p,q}(X)}=H^{q,p}(X).$$
Here $H^{p,q}(X)$ is precisely the set of classes with a $d$-closed smooth
representative of type $(p,q)$, so the decomposition is independent of the
Kähler metric. Writing $\Omega_X^p$ for the sheaf of holomorphic $p$-forms (the
kernel of $\bar\partial$ on the sheaf $\mathcal A^{p,0}$ of smooth $(p,0)$-forms),
$H^{p,q}(X)$ is isomorphic to $H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$, the sheaf cohomology of
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]. The Hodge filtration
$F^a=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}H^{p,k-p}$ of $H^k(X;\mathbb C)$ equals the filtration
induced by the holomorphic-degree filtration of the de Rham complex, whose
spectral sequence has $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$ and degenerates at $E_1$.
Pullback by holomorphic maps of compact Kähler manifolds and cup product
preserve Hodge type, so $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ is a functorial rational pure Hodge
structure.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
Jacobian-criterion, ample-powers, Chern-form and comparison suppliers below.
Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex scheme of pure dimension $n\ge0$.

Then the closed points of $X$ carry a structure of **complex manifold**
$X^{\mathrm{an}}$, its **analytification**: if $X\ne\varnothing$ and $n\ge1$
this is a compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth complex manifold of complex
dimension $n$
([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]); if $n=0$ it is the
finite discrete set $X(\mathbb C)$ with its unique complex structure in the
convention of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]; and if
$X=\varnothing$ then $X^{\mathrm{an}}=\varnothing$. Every standard smooth
algebraic chart of $X$ becomes a holomorphic chart of $X^{\mathrm{an}}$, and
every morphism of smooth complex schemes $X\to Y$ induces a holomorphic map
$X^{\mathrm{an}}\to Y^{\mathrm{an}}$.

Moreover, for every ample invertible sheaf $A$ on $X$ there is a smooth
positive closed real $(1,1)$-form $\eta_A$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ whose de Rham
class is the real image of the topological first Chern class
$c_1(A):=c_1(A^{\mathrm{an}})\in H^2(X^{\mathrm{an}};\mathbb Z)$:
$$J_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}[\eta_A]=\rho_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\bigl(c_1(A)\bigr),$$
where $J$ is the de Rham comparison and $\rho$ the change of coefficients
$\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R$
([[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]]).
In dimension $n=0$ and for $X=\varnothing$ every $2$-form and every degree-two
cohomology class is zero and $\eta_A=0$, so the identity holds trivially.

Throughout this page, assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]): the
analytic and cohomological suppliers invoked by the results below assume full
AC, and each item records its exact use. The definitional content below uses no
choice.

**(1) Compact Kähler manifolds.** Let $n\ge1$. A **Kähler manifold** is a complex
manifold $X$ of complex dimension $n$
([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]) with complex structure
$J$ and a **Hermitian metric** $g$ — a Riemannian metric
([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]) satisfying
$g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)$ for all tangent vectors $v,w$ — whose **real fundamental form**
$\omega(v,w)=g(Jv,w)$ is

- a smooth real 2-form, the section of $\Lambda^2T^*X$ obtained by alternating
  $g(J\cdot,\cdot)$;
- **positive**: $\omega(v,Jv)=g(Jv,Jv)>0$ for every nonzero tangent vector $v$;
- **closed**: $d\omega=0$.

The manifold is **compact Kähler** when the topological space $X$ is compact.

**Orientation.** For a complex basis $(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ of a tangent space $T_xX$,
the ordered real basis $(v_1,Jv_1,\dots,v_n,Jv_n)$ is declared **positive**. This
is well defined: two complex bases differ by a complex-linear automorphism, whose
real determinant is the square of the modulus of its complex determinant and so
is positive, and the local orientations therefore glue along holomorphic charts
to a global orientation of $X$. Let $v_1,\dots,v_n$ be a $g$-orthonormal complex
frame, so that $g(v_j,v_k)=\delta_{jk}$, and let $e_j=g(v_j,\cdot)$ and
$f_j=g(Jv_j,\cdot)$ be the metric-dual covectors. Then
$(e_1,f_1,\dots,e_n,f_n)$ is a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe,
$f_j=-Je_j$ for the pullback action $(J\alpha)(v)=\alpha(Jv)$ of $J$ on
covectors, and

$$\omega=\sum_{j=1}^n e_j\wedge f_j .$$

The **oriented volume form** is the top form

$$dV:=\frac{\omega^n}{n!}=e_1\wedge f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_n\wedge f_n ,$$

which evaluates to $1$ on each positively oriented $g$-orthonormal frame.

**Complex dimension zero.** For $n=0$ a complex manifold is a discrete space and
compactness makes it a finite set of points with its unique complex structure;
there are no tangent vectors and no forms of positive degree, $\omega=0$, and the
operators $L,\Lambda,\partial,\bar\partial,d,\partial^*,\bar\partial^*,d^*$ and
all Laplacians introduced below are zero. The Hodge star is the identity on
degree zero, and $dV$ is the counting measure.

**(2) Complex-valued forms and Kähler operators.** Let $X$ be compact Kähler.
Write $\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)$ for the complex-valued smooth $k$-forms, the
complex-linear extension of the real forms of
[[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]; the Hodge star $*$ of
[[def-riemannian-hodge-star]] extends complex-linearly, and for
$\alpha,\beta\in\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)$ the **integral inner product**

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle=\int_X\alpha\wedge*\bar\beta$$

is complex-linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second; the
integral is that of
[[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-top-form-on-an-oriented-manifold]] and
the integrand is $\lvert\alpha\rvert^2\,dV$ when $\beta=\alpha$, so the pairing
is a positive definite Hermitian form. In holomorphic charts

$$\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\Omega^{p,q}(X),\qquad d=\partial+\bar\partial ,$$

with $\partial$ and $\bar\partial$ of bidegree $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$
([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]]); the decomposition is independent
of the holomorphic chart because holomorphic chart changes preserve bidegree.

Put $L=\omega\wedge$, so that $L:\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)\to\Omega^{k+2}(X;\mathbb C)$,
and let $\Lambda,\partial^*,\bar\partial^*,d^*$ be the formal adjoints of
$L,\partial,\bar\partial,d$ with respect to $\langle\,,\rangle$; existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]], applied
to the bundle of complex-valued forms with the metric of
[[prop-riemannian-metrics-induce-metrics-on-dual-tensor-and-exterior-bundles]]
and the density $dV$. The **Laplacians** are

$$\Delta_d=dd^*+d^*d,\qquad \Delta_\partial=\partial\partial^*+\partial^*\partial,\qquad \Delta_{\bar\partial}=\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial ,$$

and $\epsilon(k)=(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}$.

**(3) Rational pure Hodge structures.** Let $k\in\mathbb Z$. A **rational pure
Hodge structure of weight $k$** is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-vector space
$V$ together with a direct-sum decomposition by $\mathbb C$-subspaces

$$V_{\mathbb C}=V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}V^{p,q},\qquad \overline{V^{p,q}}=V^{q,p},$$

where conjugation is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear involution
$v\otimes\lambda\mapsto v\otimes\bar\lambda$. The sum is finite because
$V_{\mathbb C}$ is finite dimensional, and it is direct by definition. The **Weil
operator** $C$ is the $\mathbb C$-linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathbb C}$ acting
as $i^{p-q}$ on $V^{p,q}$; the conjugation symmetry makes $C$ commute with
conjugation, so $C$ is the complexification of a $\mathbb Q$-linear endomorphism
of $V$.

A **polarization** of such a Hodge structure is a nondegenerate $\mathbb Q$-bilinear
form $Q:V\times V\to\mathbb Q$, extended $\mathbb C$-bilinearly to $V_{\mathbb C}$,
such that

- $Q(y,x)=(-1)^kQ(x,y)$ for all $x,y$;
- $Q(V^{p,q},V^{a,b})=0$ unless $(a,b)=(q,p)$;
- $h(x,y)=Q(Cx,\bar y)$ is a positive definite Hermitian form on $V_{\mathbb C}$.

A **rational sub-Hodge structure** is a $\mathbb Q$-subspace
$U\subseteq V$ with $U_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}(U_{\mathbb C}\cap V^{p,q})$.
The **Tate shift** $V(-r)$, for $r\in\mathbb Z$, keeps the underlying $\mathbb Q$-vector
space, the Weil operator and $Q$ as they are and moves the bidegrees to
$(p+r,q+r)$, so that the weight becomes $k+2r$; equivalently, $(V(-r))^{p,q}=V^{p-r,q-r}$.

Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$, let $P=\prod_{j=1}^n D_j$ and
$P'=\prod_{j=1}^n D'_j$ be finite open coordinate polydiscs such that each
closed coordinate disc $\overline{D'_j}$ is a compact subset of $D_j$. Let
$0\le p\le n$ and $1\le q\le n$, and let $\eta\in\Omega^{p,q}(P)$ be a
smooth form with $\bar\partial\eta=0$. Then there is a smooth
$\psi\in\Omega^{p,q-1}(P')$ such that
$$\bar\partial\psi=\eta|_{P'}.$$

Assume AC. Let $R$ be a commutative PID and $X,Y$ spaces such that every $H_q(Y;R)$ is a finite free $R$-module. For every $n\ge0$ the additive singular cohomology cross product gives an isomorphism
$$\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^p(X;R)\otimes_RH^q(Y;R)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^n(X\times Y;R).$$
All indices are nonnegative. The symmetric assertion holds when every $H_p(X;R)$ is finite free instead. No bound on the number of nonzero homology degrees and no finite-rank hypothesis on the singular chain groups is required.

For $n\ge1$, $\widetilde H_k(S^n;G)$ is $G$ for $k=n$ and $0$ otherwise.
For $S^0$, $\widetilde H_0(S^0;G)\cong G$ and all other reduced groups vanish.
Thus $H_0(S^n;G)\cong G$ for $n\ge1$, whereas
$H_0(S^0;G)\cong G\oplus G$.

Assume AC. For every field $k$, every space $X$, and $n\ge0$, evaluation gives a natural $k$-linear isomorphism
$$H^n(X;k)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}_k(H_n(X;k),k).$$
There is no finite-dimensional hypothesis. The right side is the full algebraic dual.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a metric space
([[def-metric-space]]) having a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets at
every point, and let $k$ be a field. Write $k_X$ for its constant sheaf. There
are natural isomorphisms
$$H^q(X,k_X)\cong H^q_{\operatorname{sing}}(X;k)$$
in every degree, where the left side is derived cohomology in the category of
sheaves of $k$-vector spaces (computed with the functorial $k$-linear injective
resolutions supplied by
[[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]; compare
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The same assertion holds on
every open subset of $X$. In particular a nonempty contractible space with this
local property has constant-sheaf cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero
otherwise. This applies to every finite-polyhedral open star and to its
nonempty intersection with a closed simplex.

A **rational mixed Hodge structure** consists of a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $H$
with a finite basis ([[def-linear-basis]]) together with

- a finite increasing filtration $W$ of $H$, the **weight filtration**, and
- a finite decreasing filtration $F$ of
  $H_{\mathbb C}:=H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$, the **Hodge filtration**
  ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),

such that the following opposition condition holds on every weight-graded
piece. Here a filtration is **finite** when $W_aH=0$ for all sufficiently
negative $a$ and $W_aH=H$ for all sufficiently positive $a$, and dually
$F^aH_{\mathbb C}=H_{\mathbb C}$ for $a\ll0$ and $F^aH_{\mathbb C}=0$ for
$a\gg0$ ([[def-increasing-and-decreasing-filtration-of-an-object]]).

**Conjugation.** The $\mathbb{Q}$-linear involution $\sigma$ of
$H_{\mathbb C}$, defined on generators by
$\sigma(h\otimes z)=h\otimes\bar z$ and extended $\mathbb{Q}$-linearly,
satisfies $\sigma^2=\mathrm{id}$ and $\sigma(cz)=\bar c\,\sigma(z)$ for
$c\in\mathbb C$ ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]). It preserves the
subspace $W_aH_{\mathbb C}:=(W_aH)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$ for every $a$,
so it descends to each graded piece
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH_{\mathbb C}:=W_aH_{\mathbb C}/W_{a-1}H_{\mathbb C}$
([[def-associated-graded-object-of-a-filtered-object]]). The **conjugate
Hodge filtration** is $\bar F^q:=\sigma(F^q)$, a finite decreasing filtration
of $H_{\mathbb C}$.

**Opposition.** Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-vector space with
finite decreasing filtrations $F$ and $\bar F$, and let $n$ be an integer. The
two filtrations are **$n$-opposed** when the natural map
$$\bigoplus_{p+q=n}\bigl(F^pV\cap\bar F^qV\bigr)\longrightarrow V,\qquad (v_{p,q})_{p+q=n}\longmapsto\sum_{p+q=n}v_{p,q},$$
is an isomorphism. Applied to $V=\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ this
condition is required for every $n$, with the *induced* filtrations: $F^p$
acts on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ through the image of
$F^p\cap W_nH_{\mathbb C}$, and $\bar F^q$ through the image of
$\bar F^q\cap W_nH_{\mathbb C}$. Writing
$$H^{p,q}_n:=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}\cap \bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C},$$
the requirement is therefore the direct sum decomposition
$$\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n \qquad\text{for every }n\in\mathbb Z .$$
Since $\sigma$ interchanges the induced filtrations $F^p$ and $\bar F^p$ and
preserves $W$, it maps $H^{p,q}_n$ onto $H^{q,p}_n$, so
$\overline{H^{p,q}_n}=H^{q,p}_n$. Equivalently, the opposition condition requires both
$F^pV\cap\bar F^qV=0$ whenever $p+q>n$ and
$F^pV+\bar F^{n+1-p}V=V$ for every $p$, on
$V=\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$. The conjunction, rather than either
condition alone, is equivalent to the displayed decomposition: the spanning
condition and the modular law give
$F^pV=F^{p+1}V+(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$, and the vanishing condition makes
this sum direct; descending induction through the finite filtration gives
$F^pV=\bigoplus_{a\ge p}(F^aV\cap\bar F^{n-a}V)$ and then the decomposition
of $V$. Conversely, the decomposition gives these two conditions by grouping
its summands by the first and second indices.

**Morphisms.** A morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures
is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear map with $f(W_aH)\subseteq W_aK$ for all $a$ and
$f_{\mathbb C}(F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq F^pK_{\mathbb C}$ for all $p$, where
$f_{\mathbb C}=f\otimes\mathrm{id}$. Such an $f$ commutes with the
conjugations $\sigma$, hence also satisfies
$f_{\mathbb C}(\bar F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq\bar F^pK_{\mathbb C}$.

**Substructures, pure structures, Tate.** A subspace $H'\subseteq H$ with the
induced filtrations $W_aH'=H'\cap W_aH$ and
$F^pH'_{\mathbb C}=H'_{\mathbb C}\cap F^pH_{\mathbb C}$ is a **substructure**
when the induced filtrations again satisfy the opposition condition on every
graded piece, and a quotient $H\to Q$ with the quotient filtrations is a
**quotient structure** under the same requirement; that the kernel, image and
cokernel of a morphism do carry such structures is not part of the definition
and is proved in the strictness lemma below. A structure is **pure of weight
$n$** when $W_{n-1}H=0$ and $W_nH=H$; the opposition condition then says that
$H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}$ with
$H^{p,q}=F^p\cap\bar F^q$, and $\overline{H^{p,q}}=H^{q,p}$. The **Tate
structure** $\mathbb Q(r)$, for $r\in\mathbb Z$, is the pure structure of
weight $-2r$ with $\mathbb Q(r)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ concentrated in type
$(-r,-r)$, that is $H^{-r,-r}=\mathbb C$ and $H^{p,q}=0$ for
$(p,q)\ne(-r,-r)$.

**Tensor and dual conventions.** The tensor product $H\otimes K$ carries
$$W_a(H\otimes K)=\sum_{b+c=a}W_bH\otimes W_cK,\qquad F^p(H\otimes K)_{\mathbb C}=\sum_{b+c=p}F^bH_{\mathbb C}\otimes F^cK_{\mathbb C},$$
where the sums of subspaces are those of the complexifications, and the dual
$H^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(H,\mathbb Q)$ carries
$$W_aH^*=\{u:u(W_{-a-1}H)=0\},\qquad F^pH^*_{\mathbb C}=\{u:u(F^{1-p}H_{\mathbb C})=0\}.$$

**Polarizability.** A pure rational Hodge structure $H$ of weight $n$ is
**polarizable** when it carries a rational bilinear form $Q$ of parity
$(-1)^n$ that pairs only complementary Hodge types, i.e.
$Q(H^{p,q},H^{p',q'})=0$ unless $p'=n-p$ and $q'=n-q$, and whose
Weil-operator Hermitian form $h(u,v):=Q(Cu,\bar v)$, where the Weil operator
$C$ acts as $i^{p-q}$ on $H^{p,q}$, is positive definite.

No mixed structure in this definition is assumed to split over $\mathbb R$ or
over $\mathbb Q$; the Deligne splitting constructed below is a decomposition
over $\mathbb C$ only.

A **rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex** consists of

(a) a bounded-below cochain complex $K_{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$-vector
spaces with an increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes, finite on each
cochain group;

(b) a cochain complex $K_{\mathbb C}$ of $\mathbb C$-vector spaces with an
increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes and a decreasing filtration $F$ by
subcomplexes, again finite on each cochain group;

(c) a morphism of complexes
$\alpha\colon K_{\mathbb Q}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C\to K_{\mathbb C}$
compatible with the weight filtrations, such that for every $w$ the induced map
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_w\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism,

subject to the following axiom: for every integer $w$ the weight-graded
complex $\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK$ has finite-dimensional cohomology, its
differential (induced by $d_K$) is strict for the induced filtration $F$, and
for every $r$ the induced filtration $F$ on
$H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK_{\mathbb C})$, together with the induced rational
comparison
$H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK_{\mathbb Q})\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C\to
H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK_{\mathbb C})$, is a pure Hodge structure of weight
$r+w$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

Here a cochain complex is a complex in the sense of
[[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], a filtration by subcomplexes is
a filtered complex in the sense of [[def-filtered-chain-complex]], a morphism
compatible with the weight filtrations is a filtered chain map in the sense of
[[def-filtered-chain-map]], quasi-isomorphism means
[[def-quasi-isomorphism]], and finiteness on a cochain group $K^n$ means
$W_aK^n=0$ for all sufficiently negative $a$ and $W_aK^n=K^n$ for all
sufficiently positive $a$, with bounds depending on $n$; dually $F^pK^n=K^n$
for $p\ll0$ and $F^pK^n=0$ for $p\gg0$.

**The weight filtration on cohomology** is the shifted image filtration
$$W_mH^n(K):=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K)\bigr).$$
The shift is essential: it is what makes the axiom's weight $r+w$ on the graded
complexes compatible with the weight of $H^n$, and pole-count weight on a
logarithmic complex is not the weight on its cohomology. The differential
strictness in the axiom is Deligne's condition (GH1); the equivalent
formulation that the $F$-spectral sequence of the graded complex degenerates at
its first page is recorded in the sources but is neither asserted nor used
here, so no degeneration theorem enters this definition.

**Morphisms and the sheaf case.** A morphism of cohomological mixed Hodge
complexes is a pair of chain maps $K_{\mathbb Q}\to L_{\mathbb Q}$ and
$K_{\mathbb C}\to L_{\mathbb C}$ compatible with both filtrations and with the
comparisons; compatible filtered homotopies are permitted. The same
definitions apply to bounded-below complexes of sheaves on a topological space
when the complexes are replaced by their derived global sections and the
resolutions used preserve the graded pieces; the existence of such resolutions
for the concrete complexes used later is proved where those complexes are
constructed, not here.

(i) Let $K$ be a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex
([[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]]). Then for every $n$ the vector
space $H^n(K_{\mathbb Q})$ carries a mixed Hodge structure whose weight
filtration is the shifted image filtration
$W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K))$ and whose Hodge
filtration is the image filtration
$F^pH^n(K_{\mathbb C})=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^pK_{\mathbb C})\to H^n(K_{\mathbb C}))$.
In the weight spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-p}K)$
one has $E_1^{p,q}$ pure of weight $q$, the sequence degenerates at $E_2$, and
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(K)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$ compatibly with the Hodge
filtrations. A morphism of cohomological mixed Hodge complexes induces, on
every $H^n$, a morphism of the resulting mixed Hodge structures.

(ii) Let $K^\bullet$ be a cosimplicial system of weight-zero rational Hodge
complexes concentrated in nonnegative cohomological degrees: cochain complexes
$K^{p,q}$ with coface maps and an internal differential satisfying the
cosimplicial identities, with $K^{p,q}=0$ unless $p,q\ge0$, whose differentials
are strict for the Hodge filtration, and with $H^q(K^p)$, together with the
induced $F$ and the rational comparison, a pure Hodge structure of weight $q$
for all $p,q$ (the axioms (GH1)-(GH2) of a cohomological Hodge complex of
weight zero). Form its simple
complex $sK$ with the standard total differential and the increasing filtration
$L$ by cosimplicial degree, $L_{-p}sK^n=\bigoplus_{i\ge p}K^{i,n-i}$. Then $sK$
is a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex for the filtration $L$ and the
Hodge filtrations of the $K^p$, the cosimplicial spectral sequence
$E_1^{p,q}=H^q(K^p)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(sK)$ degenerates at $E_2$, and
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$; consequently all weights of
$H^n(sK)$ are at most $n$.

Every morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures is strict for
$W$ and for $F$:
$$f(W_nH)=f(H)\cap W_nK,\qquad f(F^pH_{\mathbb C})=f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^pK_{\mathbb C}$$
for all $n,p$. Its kernel, image and cokernel, with the induced or quotient
filtrations, are mixed Hodge structures; the functor $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ is
exact; and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ (that is
$W_{n-1}H=0$) to a structure of weights at most $n$ (that is $W_nK=K$) has
pure image of weight $n$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix a topological space $X$, let
$$\Gamma(X,-):\mathrm{Ab}(X)\to\mathbf{Ab}$$
be the additive left exact global-sections functor
([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]]), and let $I$ be the supplied
functorial injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ of
[[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]]: it assigns to every abelian
sheaf $\mathcal F$ one specific injective resolution
$0\to\mathcal F\to I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$
([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]).

For every $q\ge0$ and every abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ define the
**$q$-th sheaf cohomology group of $\mathcal F$** to be the right derived
object of $\Gamma(X,-)$ relative to $I$:
$$H^q(X,\mathcal F):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)=H^q\bigl(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr),$$
the cohomology object of the complex
$\Gamma(X,I^0(\mathcal F))\to\Gamma(X,I^1(\mathcal F))\to\cdots$ of abelian
groups obtained from the deleted resolution
([[def-deleted-resolution]], [[def-cohomology-object-of-a-cochain-complex]]).
We also set $H^q(X,\mathcal F):=0$ for $q<0$.

Because $I$ is a fixed supplied datum, the group $H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ is a
specific group for each pair $(X,\mathcal F)$, and for a morphism
$\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian sheaves we write
$H^q(X,\varphi):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ for the induced map; it is the map on
cohomology induced by $\Gamma(X,-)$ applied to the cochain maps supplied with
the datum, and it is additive in $\varphi$.

If $J$ is another supplied injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ then
$R_I^q\Gamma(X,-)$ and $R_J^q\Gamma(X,-)$ are naturally isomorphic, so the
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ computed from $J$ agree with the ones above up to a
canonical natural isomorphism; the Axiom of Dependent Choice needed for that
comparison follows from AC
([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]],
[[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). The notation
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ therefore does not depend on the datum used, up to this
canonical isomorphism, and we call $q$ the **cohomological degree**.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, and let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space. Then
the abelian category $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules has
enough injectives: every $\mathcal O_X$-module embeds into an injective
$\mathcal O_X$-module, and the functorial injective embedding supplied by the
Grothendieck injective-embedding theorem for Grothendieck categories supplies,
by iteration of cokernels, one specific injective resolution
$$0\to\mathcal F\to I^0(\mathcal F)\to I^1(\mathcal F)\to\cdots$$
to each $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ with no further selection
([[def-injective-resolution-in-an-abelian-category]]). The Axiom of Choice
enters exactly through that embedding theorem applied to
$\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$; the category-theoretic verification below is
choice-free.

Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, i.e. a classical
algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), regarded as
a topological space with its analytic topology
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]), and
let $k$ be a field. Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is
an abelian category ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]), so its
bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is defined with the
conventions of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], under the
standing smallness hypothesis recorded there.

The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ consisting of the complexes $A$ satisfying:

1. $A$ is **cohomologically bounded**: $H^j(A)=0$ for $|j|$ sufficiently large;
   and
2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth
   algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$
   ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such
   that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the
   restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank
   ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent
sheaves. We use the shift convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A
groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through
an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

Constructibility is a condition on the cohomology sheaves of a complex, and it
is quantified existentially over finite smooth algebraic frontier
stratifications: no stratification is fixed, and no existence or
common-refinement theorem for stratifications is asserted by this definition.
Shifting replaces $H^j$ by $H^{j+m}$, which preserves cohomological boundedness
and shifts a witnessing stratification nowhere, so the class is closed under
shifts and under isomorphisms in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. No choice
principle is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a metric space
([[def-metric-space]]) having a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets at
every point, and let $k$ be a field. Write $k_X$ for its constant sheaf. There
are natural isomorphisms
$$H^q(X,k_X)\cong H^q_{\operatorname{sing}}(X;k)$$
in every degree, where the left side is derived cohomology in the category of
sheaves of $k$-vector spaces (computed with the functorial $k$-linear injective
resolutions supplied by
[[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]; compare
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The same assertion holds on
every open subset of $X$. In particular a nonempty contractible space with this
local property has constant-sheaf cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero
otherwise. This applies to every finite-polyhedral open star and to its
nonempty intersection with a closed simplex.

Assume AC. Every smooth quasiprojective complex variety $U$ admits a smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ with reduced boundary a simple normal crossings divisor $D$. Given finitely many such compactifications, there is another dominating all of them and restricting to the identity on $U$. A morphism of smooth quasiprojective varieties extends to a morphism of such compactifications after modifying the source compactification outside its open variety.

Assume AC. Let $p:X'\to X$ be a proper morphism between smooth projective complex varieties of equal pure dimension, restricting to the identity on a common open variety $U$. Then $H^n(X,\mathbb Q)$ and $H^n(X',\mathbb Q)$ have the same image in $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$ for every $n$. Consequently the compactification-image formula of logarithmic weights extends from an SNC compactification to every smooth projective compactification.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

For $n\ge1$, $\widetilde H_k(S^n;G)$ is $G$ for $k=n$ and $0$ otherwise.
For $S^0$, $\widetilde H_0(S^0;G)\cong G$ and all other reduced groups vanish.

$H_0(S^0;G)\cong G\oplus G$.

Assume AC. For every field $k$, every space $X$, and $n\ge0$, evaluation gives a natural $k$-linear isomorphism
$$H^n(X;k)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}_k(H_n(X;k),k).$$
There is no finite-dimensional hypothesis. The right side is the full algebraic dual.

Assume AC. Let $U$ be smooth quasiprojective over $\mathbb C$, and choose an SNC smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, boundary $D$. The logarithmic de Rham complex with Hodge filtration by degree and pole-count weight filtration constructs a functorial rational mixed Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$, independent of the compactification. Its weights are at least $n$, and
$$W_nH^n(U,\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^n(U,\mathbb Q)).$$

A **rational mixed Hodge structure** consists of a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $H$
with a finite basis ([[def-linear-basis]]) together with

- a finite increasing filtration $W$ of $H$, the **weight filtration**, and
- a finite decreasing filtration $F$ of
  $H_{\mathbb C}:=H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$, the **Hodge filtration**
  ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),

such that the following opposition condition holds on every weight-graded
piece. Here a filtration is **finite** when $W_aH=0$ for all sufficiently
negative $a$ and $W_aH=H$ for all sufficiently positive $a$, and dually
$F^aH_{\mathbb C}=H_{\mathbb C}$ for $a\ll0$ and $F^aH_{\mathbb C}=0$ for
$a\gg0$ ([[def-increasing-and-decreasing-filtration-of-an-object]]).

**Conjugation.** The $\mathbb{Q}$-linear involution $\sigma$ of
$H_{\mathbb C}$, defined on generators by
$\sigma(h\otimes z)=h\otimes\bar z$ and extended $\mathbb{Q}$-linearly,
satisfies $\sigma^2=\mathrm{id}$ and $\sigma(cz)=\bar c\,\sigma(z)$ for
$c\in\mathbb C$ ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]). It preserves the
subspace $W_aH_{\mathbb C}:=(W_aH)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$ for every $a$,
so it descends to each graded piece
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH_{\mathbb C}:=W_aH_{\mathbb C}/W_{a-1}H_{\mathbb C}$
([[def-associated-graded-object-of-a-filtered-object]]). The **conjugate
Hodge filtration** is $\bar F^q:=\sigma(F^q)$, a finite decreasing filtration
of $H_{\mathbb C}$.

**Opposition.** Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-vector space with
finite decreasing filtrations $F$ and $\bar F$, and let $n$ be an integer. The
two filtrations are **$n$-opposed** when the natural map
$$\bigoplus_{p+q=n}\bigl(F^pV\cap\bar F^qV\bigr)\longrightarrow V,\qquad (v_{p,q})_{p+q=n}\longmapsto\sum_{p+q=n}v_{p,q},$$
is an isomorphism. Applied to $V=\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ this
condition is required for every $n$, with the *induced* filtrations: $F^p$
acts on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ through the image of
$F^p\cap W_nH_{\mathbb C}$, and $\bar F^q$ through the image of
$\bar F^q\cap W_nH_{\mathbb C}$. Writing
$$H^{p,q}_n:=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}\cap \bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C},$$
the requirement is therefore the direct sum decomposition
$$\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n \qquad\text{for every }n\in\mathbb Z .$$
Since $\sigma$ interchanges the induced filtrations $F^p$ and $\bar F^p$ and
preserves $W$, it maps $H^{p,q}_n$ onto $H^{q,p}_n$, so
$\overline{H^{p,q}_n}=H^{q,p}_n$. Equivalently, the opposition condition requires both
$F^pV\cap\bar F^qV=0$ whenever $p+q>n$ and
$F^pV+\bar F^{n+1-p}V=V$ for every $p$, on
$V=\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$. The conjunction, rather than either
condition alone, is equivalent to the displayed decomposition: the spanning
condition and the modular law give
$F^pV=F^{p+1}V+(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$, and the vanishing condition makes
this sum direct; descending induction through the finite filtration gives
$F^pV=\bigoplus_{a\ge p}(F^aV\cap\bar F^{n-a}V)$ and then the decomposition
of $V$. Conversely, the decomposition gives these two conditions by grouping
its summands by the first and second indices.

**Morphisms.** A morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures
is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear map with $f(W_aH)\subseteq W_aK$ for all $a$ and
$f_{\mathbb C}(F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq F^pK_{\mathbb C}$ for all $p$, where
$f_{\mathbb C}=f\otimes\mathrm{id}$. Such an $f$ commutes with the
conjugations $\sigma$, hence also satisfies
$f_{\mathbb C}(\bar F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq\bar F^pK_{\mathbb C}$.

**Substructures, pure structures, Tate.** A subspace $H'\subseteq H$ with the
induced filtrations $W_aH'=H'\cap W_aH$ and
$F^pH'_{\mathbb C}=H'_{\mathbb C}\cap F^pH_{\mathbb C}$ is a **substructure**
when the induced filtrations again satisfy the opposition condition on every
graded piece, and a quotient $H\to Q$ with the quotient filtrations is a
**quotient structure** under the same requirement; that the kernel, image and
cokernel of a morphism do carry such structures is not part of the definition
and is proved in the strictness lemma below. A structure is **pure of weight
$n$** when $W_{n-1}H=0$ and $W_nH=H$; the opposition condition then says that
$H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}$ with
$H^{p,q}=F^p\cap\bar F^q$, and $\overline{H^{p,q}}=H^{q,p}$. The **Tate
structure** $\mathbb Q(r)$, for $r\in\mathbb Z$, is the pure structure of
weight $-2r$ with $\mathbb Q(r)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ concentrated in type
$(-r,-r)$, that is $H^{-r,-r}=\mathbb C$ and $H^{p,q}=0$ for
$(p,q)\ne(-r,-r)$.

**Tensor and dual conventions.** The tensor product $H\otimes K$ carries
$$W_a(H\otimes K)=\sum_{b+c=a}W_bH\otimes W_cK,\qquad F^p(H\otimes K)_{\mathbb C}=\sum_{b+c=p}F^bH_{\mathbb C}\otimes F^cK_{\mathbb C},$$
where the sums of subspaces are those of the complexifications, and the dual
$H^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(H,\mathbb Q)$ carries
$$W_aH^*=\{u:u(W_{-a-1}H)=0\},\qquad F^pH^*_{\mathbb C}=\{u:u(F^{1-p}H_{\mathbb C})=0\}.$$

**Polarizability.** A pure rational Hodge structure $H$ of weight $n$ is
**polarizable** when it carries a rational bilinear form $Q$ of parity
$(-1)^n$ that pairs only complementary Hodge types, i.e.
$Q(H^{p,q},H^{p',q'})=0$ unless $p'=n-p$ and $q'=n-q$, and whose
Weil-operator Hermitian form $h(u,v):=Q(Cu,\bar v)$, where the Weil operator
$C$ acts as $i^{p-q}$ on $H^{p,q}$, is positive definite.

No mixed structure in this definition is assumed to split over $\mathbb R$ or
over $\mathbb Q$; the Deligne splitting constructed below is a decomposition
over $\mathbb C$ only.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
